guarantees.claim: data_out_we_o, data_in_prev_we_o, ctr_incr_o, cipher_in_valid_o, cipher_out_ready_o, cipher_crypt_o, cipher_dec_key_gen_o are directly assigned via sp2v_e type conversion from their respective source sp_* signals.

alert_o, cipher_prng_reseed_o, cipher_key_clear_o, cipher_data_out_clear_o, prng_data_req_o, prng_reseed_req_o, start_we_o, prng_reseed_o, prng_reseed_we_o are assigned as the bitwise OR of the corresponding mr_* vector signals.

ctrl_we_o, data_in_we_o, key_iv_data_in_clear_we_o, data_out_clear_we_o, idle_o, idle_we_o, stall_o, stall_we_o, output_lost_o, output_lost_we_o, output_valid_o, output_valid_we_o, input_ready_o, input_ready_we_o are assigned as the bitwise AND of the corresponding mr_* vector signals.

assumptions.claim: All bits of mr_* vector signals (used in OR/AND reductions) are defined (no X) and correctly represent the intended FSM output state.
assumptions.cond: during any operational state where these outputs are observed
assumptions.risk: An X on any bit causes the reduced output (e.g., alert_o, idle_o) to be X, propagating undefined behavior; a stuck bit in OR-reduced signals can permanently assert the output (e.g., persistent alert), potentially masking further events or causing denial of service.

assumptions.claim: The sp_* signals (sp_data_out_we, sp_data_in_prev_we, sp_ctr_incr, sp_cipher_in_valid, sp_cipher_out_ready, sp_out_cipher_crypt, sp_out_cipher_dec_key_gen) carry valid sparse enum values for the sp2v_e type conversion to produce a deterministic single-bit result.
assumptions.cond: whenever these output signals are observed
assumptions.risk: If any sp_* signal is X or an illegal sparse value, sp2v_e may produce X, corrupting downstream control signals such as cipher_crypt_o or cipher_dec_key_gen_o, potentially enabling unintended cryptographic operations or invalid data transfers.

uncertain_points.claim: De-assertion of alert_o requires all bits of mr_alert to go low. If any FSM holds its alert bit high indefinitely (e.g., due to a deadlock or incorrect state clearance), alert_o will remain permanently asserted.
uncertain_points.cond: after an alert event that one FSM does not clear
uncertain_points.risk: A stuck alert can mask subsequent genuine alerts, preventing detection of security violations or errors, and may lead to unrecoverable system state.

uncertain_points.claim: If any bit of mr_idle, mr_stall, or other AND-reduced vectors becomes X, the output signal (e.g., idle_o, stall_o) becomes X, which may be interpreted incorrectly by downstream logic (e.g., as idle when not truly idle).
uncertain_points.cond: when an upstream fault or uninitialized state produces X on a mr_* bit
uncertain_points.risk: Incorrect idle/stall interpretation can lead to data corruption, protocol violations, or security bypass if critical checks are skipped.

uncertain_points.claim: The sp2v_e conversion for each sparse signal (e.g., cipher_crypt_o, cipher_dec_key_gen_o) must be fully defined and free of missing case selectors; an incomplete mapping could produce X for a legal sparse encoding.
uncertain_points.cond: when the sparse FSM outputs a legal or unexpected state value
uncertain_points.risk: X on cipher_crypt_o could cause the cipher core to enter an undefined operational mode, potentially leaking key material or corrupting output.

uncertain_points.claim: The OR reduction of cipher_key_clear_o from mr_cipher_key_clear means any FSM can trigger a key clear, but the spec does not clarify if simultaneous clear requests from different FSMs require coordinated timing or if an early clear could disrupt ongoing operations.
uncertain_points.cond: when multiple FSMs assert cipher_key_clear concurrently or at different times
uncertain_points.risk: Premature key clear could cause data underflow or security vulnerability if clearing is not purposely sequenced.
